Hi Ben / Sara,

Thanks again for taking the time today - great conversation. Quick recap and agreed next steps from our side: 

- Summary of needs: primary use is automated customer support triage + downstream extraction for fraud signals. You emphasized short, structured answers and high throughput during peak hours (monthly peak: ~1.5M messages/day).
- Near-term ask: model fit recommendations and quantified perf/cost estimates so your infra team can size Dedicated vs Hosted.
- Action items (Redwood): share model-fit recommendations, benchmark links, prompt sets we used for the evals, and Redwood-verified performance profiles (TPS and latency percentiles) scoped to your typical payloads.

I'm attaching the benchmark PDF and the prompt set we used for the eval. The quick highlights below (more detail in attachment/links):

Recommended model candidates:
- redwood-7b-chat (quantized): best latency-cost balance for production chatflows; good for structured outputs and extraction.
- redwood-13b-qa: better F1 on entity extraction tests (around +4-6%), higher cost but useful for high-accuracy paths.
- redwood-70b-qa (float16 / dedicated): top quality for rare/fuzzy fraud cases; consider only for A/B or fallback due to cost.

Quick performance snapshots (measured in our verified harness against your prompt set; full CSV attached):
- redwood-7b-chat (q4_k_mixed): TPS=320, p50=18ms, p95=54ms, p99=120ms (single-GPU, batching=32, seq=128 typical).
- redwood-13b-qa (int8): TPS=120, p50=46ms, p95=110ms, p99=240ms (single A100 pod, batching=16).
- redwood-70b-qa (fp16, multi-GPU): TPS=18, p50=210ms, p95=430ms, p99=920ms (multi-card, KV shards).

Notes on quality/regression: we saw consistent extraction F1 deltas across prompt variations; redwood-13b-qa is the safest uplift from 7b for your dataset. We'll include prompt calibration scripts so you can re-run locally.

Links & attachments: benchmark PDF + prompt_set_fintechcorp_v1.json + performance CSV included; also sharing the Drive folder and the Redwood perf profile page.

Next steps:
1) I'll loop in Alex (cc'd) to scope Dedicated sizing for a Pilot (target: 100k/day steady, spike to 1.5M/day).
2) If you want, we can send a short A/B plan: 7b in production, 13b for sampled extractions to compare quality + cost.
3) Please confirm availability for a 30-min infra sizing call next week (I'm available Tue/Wed PST).

Thanks - talk soon.

Hi Ben / Sara - great questions. Answers inline below and attached a short sizing note from Alex.

1) 7b TPS / batching: TPS=320 above was measured with our continuous-batching policy: target batch size 32, max latency cap 200ms. With your average token length (~90) we expect p95 ~60-80ms for the 7b config; p99 ~140-160ms in peak batching conditions. If you need tighter p99, we recommend reducing max batch size or using Dedicated with lower concurrency per GPU.

2) 13b p99 at 256 tokens: measured p99 ~320-360ms (single A100 pod, batching=8 for stability). We observed tail amplification with longer sequences - that's expected. For extraction tasks we suggest using a trimmed prompt template (we included prompt_set_fintechcorp_v1.json) to keep tokens lower and reduce tail effects.

3) Cost delta hosted vs dedicated (ballpark):
- redwood-7b-chat: hosted ~ $0.26 / 1k requests; dedicated amortized infra cost ~ $0.14 / 1k requests at 100k/day steady with 2.5x utilization.
- redwood-13b-qa: hosted ~ $0.75 / 1k requests; dedicated ~ $0.42 / 1k requests (depends on committed hours and instance family).
- redwood-70b-qa: steep delta - hosted is convenience-first; dedicated only makes sense at high sustained volume or for compliance.

Attached: a one-pager sizing note (Alex) that translates TPS to GPU pod counts and gives a recommended Pilot config (2x A100 dedicated for pilot with autoscale to 4x for spikes).

On quality/regression: we ran a lightweight drift check on your sample set vs public corpora - no immediate regression flags. We'll include a small eval harness (prompt + reference set) you can run against new model releases; this is how we trigger quality regression alerts inside Redwood Optimize.

Call: Wed 11am PST works for us. I'll set a calendar invite and include Alex to walk through sizing.

Best,
Marissa

Hey Ben / Sara - Alex here (runtime infra). Quick technical note to supplement Marissa's pricing/latency answers:

- Pilot recommendation: start with 2 A100s pinned to the redwood-7b-chat quantized profile with continuous batching and prefix caching. That configuration gives a good balance: the measured 320 TPS assumes batching=32 and concurrency tuned to keep avg latency in target.
- Autoscale strategy: scale by queue depth (not CPU) and cap batch size to keep p99 under 200ms for the 7b profile. For 13b, use a sampled subset routed to a dedicated pool to avoid impacting cost.
- Regression guardrails: include a lightweight eval set in CI that runs nightly against model variants; use Redwood Optimize to alert on metric dips >2.5% on F1. We can provide that harness (see prompt_set_fintechcorp_v1.json attachment).
